title: Prediction: The Most-Anticipated Stock Split of the Fourth Quarter Will Be Announced This Month | The Motley Fool
content: The Motley Fool predicts that Netflix will announce a stock split in October 2025, making it the most anticipated split of the fourth quarter. Stock splits do not alter a company’s fundamentals but often generate investor excitement and media attention. Historically, stocks that split have outperformed the S&P 500—rising 25.4% over four decades compared to the S&P’s 11.9%, according to Bank of America research—though this correlation likely reflects companies choosing splits during strong market conditions and periods of confidence. Netflix’s shares are currently trading near $1,200, one of the highest in the S&P 500, and the company is expected to report fourth-quarter earnings on October 21, 2025, a likely timing for a split announcement. Netflix has previously executed a 7-for-1 split in 2015 and a 2-for-1 split in 2004. A split would lower the share price, benefiting retail investors and potentially making Netflix eligible for inclusion in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, where it would be a rare entertainment-sector representative despite its $500 billion market cap. Although Netflix is not part of the 'Magnificent Seven,' it has outperformed many of them in recent years. Analysts forecast revenue of $11.5 billion (a 17% year-over-year increase) and earnings per share of $6.94, up from $5.40. Despite a high price-to-earnings ratio of 50, Netflix remains dominant in global video entertainment with strong growth potential driven by advertising and local content. A stock split could signal confidence and catalyze the next phase of stock appreciation.

title: 2025年8月28日　ダウ 45636.90（+71.67 +0.16%）：S＆P500 6501.86（+20.46 +0.32%）：ナスダック 21705.16（+115.02 +0.53%） - 公営競技はどこへ行く
content: On 29 August 2025, the U.S. equity market closed higher: the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished at 45 636.90, up 71.67 points (+0.16%); the S&P 500 closed at 6 501.86, up 20.46 points (+0.32%); and the Nasdaq Composite ended at 21 705.16, up 115.02 points (+0.53%). Oil futures were up 0.45 USD to 64.60 (+0.70%), gold futures rose 25.70 USD to 3 474.30 (+0.75%), and copper futures increased 4.35 USD to 453.90 (+0.97%). In currency markets, the U.S. dollar fell to 146.97 JPY (down 0.42 JPY, –0.28%) and the euro rose to 1.1678 USD (up 0.0041 USD, +0.35%). U.S. Treasury yields were largely unchanged: the 2‑year yield was 3.633% (up 0.01 pp), the 10‑year 4.205% (down 0.033 pp), and the 30‑year 4.874% (down 0.039 pp). European indices were mixed: the FTSE 100 closed at 9 216.82 (down 38.68 points, –0.42%), the DAX at 24 039.92 (down 6.29 points, –0.03%), and the CAC 40 at 7 762.6 (up 18.67 points, +0.24%). Nvidia’s earnings report, which missed some expectations, saw the stock decline 0.8% to 180.17 USD, yet analysts noted that AI‑related demand remained strong, supporting broader tech stocks. U.S. unemployment claims fell 5 000 to 229 000, below the 230 000 forecast, easing recession concerns. Market focus shifted to the upcoming PCE inflation data and the September FOMC meeting, where an 83 % probability of a rate cut was priced in. Overall, the market moved cautiously, with modest gains across major indices and a muted reaction to Nvidia’s earnings.

title: Stock market holiday: Is US stock market closed or open today for Labor Day 2025? | Stock Market News
content: The United States stock markets will remain closed on Monday, 1 September 2025, in observance of Labor Day, according to the official holiday list of the Nasdaq Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). Because the market is closed on Saturday and Sunday, there is no half‑day trading session preceding the holiday. Official NYSE data indicates that only two other holidays will occur in 2025: Thanksgiving on 27 November and Christmas on 25 December. title: Are Wall Street Analysts Bullish on Aon Stock?
content: Aon plc (AON), a global professional services firm, has underperformed the broader market over the past 52 weeks, with its shares gaining 10.7% compared to the S&P 500 Index's 16.4% rally. However, the company's second-quarter earnings showed strong execution of its Aon United strategy, with revenue surging 11% year-over-year to $4.16 billion and adjusted operating income increasing 14% to $1.17 billion. Analysts expect AON's adjusted EPS to grow 8.1% year-over-year to $16.86 in the current fiscal year, with a consensus rating of 'Moderate Buy' based on 11 'Strong Buy' ratings, one 'Moderate Buy,' seven 'Holds,' one 'Moderate Sell,' and two 'Strong Sells.' This configuration is more bullish than a month ago, with nine 'Strong Buy' ratings on the stock.
